definitions.gloss: to walk side by side; to stand alongside
definitions.explanation: Literally, to line up one's shoulders with someone — to walk or stand next to each other.

definitions.gloss: to rival; to be on par with; to equal
definitions.explanation: Figuratively, to be at the same level as someone in skill, status, or achievement. Often used to describe reaching the level of a superior competitor.

examples.japanese: {二人|ふたり}は{肩|かた}を{並|なら}べて{歩|ある}いた。
examples.english: The two walked side by side.

examples.japanese: {友人|ゆうじん}と{肩|かた}を{並|なら}べて{夕日|ゆうひ}を{眺|なが}めた。
examples.english: I watched the sunset standing alongside my friend.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}はついに{世界|せかい}のトップと{肩|かた}を{並|なら}べた。
examples.english: He finally rivaled the best in the world.

examples.japanese: この{会社|かいしゃ}は{大手|おおて}と{肩|かた}を{並|なら}べるほどの{技術力|ぎじゅつりょく}を{持|も}っている。
examples.english: This company has the technological capability to rival major corporations.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}のワインは{今|いま}や{海外|かいがい}の{有名|ゆうめい}ワインと{肩|かた}を{並|なら}べるまでになった。
examples.english: Japanese wine has now reached the point where it can stand alongside famous wines from overseas.

notes:
USAGE:
The literal meaning (sense 1) is straightforward. The figurative meaning (sense 2) is more commonly encountered and implies reaching an equal level after effort or growth. Often used with ～ほど or ～まで to emphasize the degree of achievement.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {世界|せかい}と{肩|かた}を{並|なら}べる (to rival the world's best)
- {肩|かた}を{並|なら}べて{歩|ある}く (to walk side by side)
- ～と{肩|かた}を{並|なら}べるほど (to the extent of rivaling ~)
